primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: A somatic PIGA mutation in a hematopoietic stem-cell clone impairs glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor synthesis, preventing surface attachment of complement-regulatory proteins such as CD55 and CD59 and causing complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis.
vignette: A 32-year-old woman is evaluated for recurrent fatigue, episodic dark urine, and abdominal pain. Imaging obtained for persistent abdominal pain shows hepatic vein thrombosis. Flow cytometry demonstrates a blood-cell clone with markedly reduced surface expression of CD55 and CD59.
lead: Which molecular abnormality most directly explains these findings?
correct: An acquired somatic PIGA mutation causing defective GPI-anchor synthesis
distractors: IgG autoantibodies directed against erythrocyte membrane antigens
Acquired inhibition of the von Willebrand factor–cleaving protease ADAMTS13
distractor_notes: Spectrin or related membrane-cytoskeletal protein defects cause hereditary spherocytosis, not loss of GPI-anchored CD55/CD59.
G6PD deficiency impairs NADPH and reduced-glutathione regeneration, producing oxidant-triggered hemolysis rather than a clone lacking GPI-anchored proteins.
Warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia is usually IgG-mediated erythrocyte destruction; it does not produce a multilineage GPI-anchor deficiency.
Acquired ADAMTS13 inhibition causes immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura with platelet-rich microthrombi and microangiopathic hemolysis, not CD55/CD59 loss.
key_expl: The combination of hemoglobinuria, unusual venous thrombosis, and loss of CD55/CD59 identifies paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria. Most PNH results from an acquired somatic PIGA mutation in a hematopoietic stem cell. Defective GPI-anchor synthesis prevents complement-regulatory proteins such as CD55 and CD59 from attaching to blood-cell membranes, permitting complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis.
objective: Link the hemoglobinuria/thrombosis phenotype and flow-cytometric loss of CD55/CD59 in PNH to an acquired somatic PIGA mutation that disrupts GPI-anchor synthesis.
clues: episodic dark urine from intravascular hemolysis
loss of CD55 and CD59 on flow cytometry

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes PNH as an acquired hemolytic disorder with dark urine and thrombosis, states that almost all cases involve somatic PIGA variants in hematopoietic stem cells, and explains that loss of PIG-A prevents GPI-anchor production and surface expression of protective GPI-anchored proteins.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria
sources.support: NCBI states that PIGA mutation causes GPI-anchor deficiency, prevents CD55/CD59 attachment, causes complement-mediated hemolysis, is associated with intra-abdominal/hepatic venous thrombosis, and that flow cytometry assessing GPI-anchored proteins including CD55/CD59 is the diagnostic gold standard.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Hereditary Spherocytosis
sources.support: NCBI identifies hereditary spherocytosis as a congenital hemolytic anemia caused by deficiencies in erythrocyte membrane/cytoskeletal proteins including spectrin, ankyrin, band 3, and band 4.2.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase Deficiency
sources.support: NCBI states that G6PD deficiency reduces NADPH-dependent antioxidant defense and predisposes erythrocytes to hemolysis during oxidative stress.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Laboratory Evaluation of Immune Hemolytic Anemias
sources.locator: Etiology and Epidemiology — Autoimmune hemolytic anemia
sources.support: NCBI describes warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia as predominantly IgG autoantibody-mediated erythrocyte destruction.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura
sources.support: NCBI states that acquired TTP is caused by autoantibodies that reduce ADAMTS13 activity, allowing platelet-rich microthrombi and microangiopathic hemolysis.
